header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Carter (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (Mariner Head of AI), Marcus Lee (Mariner CTO), Priya Nair (Mariner Infra), Tom Delgado (Mariner Finance)
summary: Redwood walkthrough of Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for cost predictability and data isolation; primary concerns are cost attribution per route, latency SLOs for supply-chain tracking, and compliance (SOC2/VPC). Agreed next steps include sending pricing, SOC2 docs, and running a POC benchmark with sample traffic.
transcript:
[00:00] Lina: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Lina from Redwood, AE on this account. With me are Samir and Jules from engineering.
[00:12] Elena: Hi all, Elena here. Marcus, Priya and Tom are on as well. We appreciate the time.
[00:18] Samir: Quick agenda - we'll walk the Console usage analytics, show per-route dashboards, and then do a cost breakdown. Happy to answer infra/security Qs as we go.
[00:30] Marcus: Sounds good. Our primary goal is to understand cost attribution and whether Dedicated makes sense vs hosted. Also latency to our regional nodes is key.
[00:44] Lina: Great, we'll start with the top-level usage page. So this is the Console home - you get token-level cost and latency traces by model and route.
[00:58] Jules: Note, the Console automatically attributes costs per route using tags, and you can slice by model family, quantization profile, and time window.
[01:12] Priya: Quick interjection - how do you handle burst capacity? We have big ebbs in nightly batch jobs.
[01:20] Samir: We show autoscale events and burst utilization; for Dedicated you can configure burst pools. In the Console you can see when burst was triggered and the incremental cost.
[01:34] Tom: And can we map that back to a ledger line for accounting? That is, per-route dollar amount?
[01:42] Lina: Yes - per-route billing exports. We can export CSV/Parquet with token counts, model variant, quantization, and cost allocation per route/id.
[01:58] Elena: When you say model variant, does that include quantized variants? We plan to run mixed precision for cheaper cost.
[02:06] Jules: Yes, the Console differentiates variant: full-precision, int8 quantizashun (sic), and sparse variants. The cost model shows per-token and aggregated cost.
[02:22] Marcus: Show us the per-route dashboard for our 'tracking-sync' route. That is our main latency-sensitive path.
[02:30] Samir: Pulling it up - here you see request rate, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and token breakdown. The top chart is p95 over the last 30 days.
[02:48] Lina: You'll notice we also show KV cache hit rate (transcript sometimes says KV cash) - that reduces token counts.
[02:58] Priya: That KV cache is one of the big levers for us - can you show how it impacts cost?
[03:06] Jules: Sure, overlaying cache hit rate on token spend. For this route, when hit rate goes from 10% to 60% we saw token spend drop ~40%.
[03:18] Elena: How do you instrument route tagging? We have services that call different prompts, want them mapped automatically.
[03:26] Samir: You can set route tags at the SDK or API layer - route.name/service tags. The Console can also infer from headers if you enable automatic attribution.
[03:39] Marcus: On security - we have to keep logs off-premise, and need KMS integration.
[03:45] Samir: For Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS, and audit logs can be forward to your SIEM. SOC2 documentation is available - we'll share the latest report.
[03:58] Tom: Any notes about data residency? We need EU-only for some customers.
[04:04] Lina: You can pin routing to region, or use Private deployment with VPC and on-prem options for strict residency.
[04:14] Elena: Back to cost - show the cost breakdown widget.
[04:20] Jules: Here, we have cost by model, by route, and by quantization. You can drill into a single route and see per-request cost. The Console supports showing amortized GPU hours for Dedicated as an additional view.
[04:36] Marcus: Can we see a hypothetical switch to int8 on this route?
[04:40] Samir: Yes - simulate mode. You pick the variant and it estimates token cost, latency delta, and QoE risk. For this route switching to int8 cuts cost ~35% but p95 increases ~12ms in this example.
[04:56] Priya: That's great. What's the typical accuracy regressions you see after quantization?
[05:02] Jules: It depends on model and prompt; the Console ties into Optimize which suggests quant profiles and runs small evals. We highlight example regressions and let you accept or reject.
[05:16] Elena: Do you support function calling and streaming in the cost model? Streaming sometimes uses more tokens due to retries.
[05:24] Samir: Yes - streaming tokens are counted, and the billing export includes token type (prompt/completion/stream). Retries show up as additional requests; Console flags high retry patterns.
[05:38] Marcus: Let's talk Dedicated pricing - where do we see amortized cost vs hosted?
[05:44] Lina: In Console you can compare hosted per-token spend vs Dedicated amortized GPU + infra. We provide a cost model spreadsheet you can upload your traffic to; Jules will prepare a sample.
[06:00] Tom: For accounting, we need an export that groups charges by GL code. Can you customize exports?
[06:08] Jules: Exports are configurable; you can add custom route tags that map to GL codes. The CSV will include tag columns.
[06:18] Elena: Any integrations for our billing system? We use NetLedger.
[06:22] Lina: We have S3 exports and webhooks; customers typically load into NetLedger via an ETL job.
[06:30] Marcus: On latency - our SLO is 95th < 120ms for that route. How do we validate?
[06:36] Samir: Console tracing shows per-request traces; you can filter by model and region. For Dedicated we guarantee latency under certain SLAs - we'll share SLA doc.
[06:48] Priya: For POC, we want to run a synthetic benchmark plus a replay of a day's traffic. Is that feasible?
[06:55] Jules: Absolutely - we can run a replay in a sandbox Dedicated pool and produce the same Console dashboards for comparison.
[07:04] Elena: How long is a POC typically?
[07:07] Lina: Usually 2 weeks to get meaningful numbers; for your traffic pattern we suggested 1-2 weeks of replay plus live test.
[07:15] Tom: Cost of POC?
[07:17] Lina: POC pricing depends on Dedicated capacity; we usually offer credits, but we'll include exact terms in the pricing doc.
[07:28] Marcus: Any compliance red flags?
[07:30] Samir: No major blockers - VPC, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC are supported. There are some network egress considerations for on-prem. We'll review with your security team.
[07:46] Elena: Can you show the routing policy view? We sometimes want automatic fallback to cheaper models on high load.
[07:54] Jules: Here's the policy editor - you can route by latency, cost, region or customer tier. Fallback to smaller variants is supported and the Console shows risk/expected quality impact.
[08:08] Marcus: If fallback triggers, do we get traces of which model served which request?
[08:12] Samir: Yes - every request has model metadata; Console traces show the selected variant and why the policy chose it.
[08:22] Priya: About caching - do you do prefix caching? We have deterministic prompts for many calls.
[08:28] Jules: We support prefix/KV caching and automatic cache keys. The Console surfaces cache hit/miss and estimated token savings.
[08:38] Elena: Any gotchas around privacy when caching?
[08:41] Samir: You control what is cached and whether cache is encrypted; for Private deployments cache can be customer-managed.
[08:50] Tom: Can you demo the per-route cost drilldown for the last 30 days?
[08:56] Jules: Sure - zooming into route, here's daily token counts, model split, and dollar cost. Notice the spike on Nov 28 - that's an atypical batch job.
[09:12] Marcus: Hmm, can we set alerts for anomalous spend?
[09:16] Lina: Yes - Console supports spend alerts, rate-based alerts, and quality regression alerts. Can send to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhooks.
[09:28] Elena: For our audit we need retention of usage logs for 12 months. Can Console hold that?
[09:34] Samir: Retention is configurable; hosted plans have tiers, Dedicated can retain locally longer, and Private you manage retention. We'll include retention options in the docs.
[09:48] Marcus: Walk me through a sample CSV export column set.
[09:52] Jules: Columns: timestamp, request_id, route_tag, model_variant, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, quant_profile, cost_usd, region, customer_tag, GL_code (if provided), KV_cache_hit.
[10:08] Tom: Great. For our finance team we'll need the GL_code mapping set up before POC.
[10:14] Lina: Noted; Jules will include a sample with GL columns for you to map.
[10:22] Elena: Any limitations with streaming/long-running sessions?
[10:26] Samir: Long sessions maintain KV cache and token accounting; Console shows session-level token accumulations. There are some session size limits per model but we can advise.
[10:40] Marcus: On model upgrades - if we pin a version and you roll a backward-incompatible change, how do we handle rollouts?
[10:48] Jules: Console supports canary rollouts and A/B tests by route; you can pin model versions and the routing layer will respect that. We also provide automatic fallback policies.
[11:04] Elena: Let's talk about the POC checklist.
[11:07] Lina: Checklist: share traffic sample, agree on routes and SLOs, pick test window, get account access, run replay, analyze Console dashboards, validate cost model.
[11:20] Tom: Who owns the replay? We prefer to keep data off Redwood infra during initial test.
[11:26] Samir: We can run replay in your VPC with Private deployment or in a sandbox Dedicated pool; both options possible.
[11:36] Marcus: Regarding SLA - what uptime and latency guarantees for Dedicated?
[11:40] Lina: We provide SLA terms per contract; typical uptime commitments are 99.9% for Dedicated with latency SLOs included. We'll send exact SLA language.
[11:54] Elena: Any references from logistics customers?
[11:58] Lina: We can share redacted case studies; we'll include a logistics reference that has similar bursty traffic patterns.
[12:06] Priya: For the POC dataset, we need guidance on anonymization. Any best practices?
[12:12] Jules: Strip PII, use realistic but synthetic IDs for replay; we can provide a small script for masking.
[12:22] Tom: About cost - if Dedicated has reserved capacity, do you offer burst billing outside commit?
[12:28] Lina: Yes, burst pools are billed on usage but at a different rate; we'll include examples in the pricing spreadsheet.
[12:38] Marcus: Are there any hidden costs we should be aware of? e.g., data egress, storage of cache, logging retention?
[12:46] Jules: Egress and extended retention can add cost. We include these line items in the cost model so you can map to GL accounts.
[12:56] Elena: Show the Optimize suggestions for this route.
[13:00] Samir: Optimize recommends batching settings, a cache TTL, and a quant profile. It gives estimated savings and quality risk.
[13:12] Priya: What's the typical saving from batching?
[13:15] Jules: Depends on latency tolerance; continuous batching can reduce per-token cost up to 30% for high-RPS routes.
[13:24] Marcus: For our latency-sensitive route we can't batch much, but maybe for background summaries we can.
[13:29] Lina: Right - Console helps you pick which routes to optimize aggressively.
[13:38] Tom: Any thoughts on forecasting cost as volume grows?
[13:42] Jules: Console has forecasting based on historical usage and seasonality. You can plug in growth assumptions.
[13:50] Elena: Okay, can you show again the per-route cost split and then we'll move to next steps?
[13:56] Jules: Drilling one more time - you can see daily, model split, token-type, and net cost. Exports available.
[14:12] Marcus: Good. On the integrations side, we need the ingestion headers and SDK sample to set route tags.
[14:18] Samir: We'll send SDK snippets. Also note that auto-attribution uses a specific header 'x-rd-route' in our SDKs.
[14:30] Priya: For resilience, do you support multi-region active-active?
[14:34] Samir: Yes - routing supports region affinity and active-active deployments with sticky KV caches and replication considerations.
[14:48] Elena: Any latency penalty for active-active?
[14:52] Jules: Slight replication overhead for KV cache; we recommend local cache with async replicate for most workloads.
[15:04] Marcus: Let's summarize next steps.
[15:07] Lina: Action items recap: Lina will send pricing and Dedicated SKUs; Samir will share SOC2 and VPC diagram; Jules will prepare sample usage export and cost spreadsheet; Mariner to provide traffic sample and GL mappings. We'll schedule POC week of Dec 13.
[15:26] Tom: Thanks, seems good.
[15:29] Elena: Thanks all.
[15:32] Samir: One last note - we'll include a simulated cost-run for switching main route to int8 in the deliverables.
[15:40] Lina: Great. We'll follow up via email with docs and a calendar invite for the POC prep call.
[41:30] <end of recording>
